chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Miskeen ibn Abu al-Hakam from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he looked at the greying in his beard. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Radiance.' Then he said: 'Whoever grows grey in Islam, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection.'

He said: So the man dyed with henna, then he came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). When he saw the dyeing, he said: 'Radiance and Islam.' The man then dyed with black, so the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Radiance and Islam and faith and love for your wives and awe in the hearts of your enemies.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of dyeing the beard according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the Sunnah of beautifying the beard, distinguishing between the natural 'light' of grey hair and the spiritual merit of dyeing it. While henna is praised for its simplicity and connection to Islam, black dye is elevated as a sign of faith (Iman) and love for wives, while also instilling awe in enemies, reflecting the Shia emphasis on outward appearance as an extension of inner piety.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yaha, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Miskeen Bin Abu Al Hakam, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> saw the greying in his beard. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who gets old and grey in Al-Islam, there would be a radiance for him on the Day of Judgement’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So the man dyed with the henna, then he came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So when he<sup>saww</sup> saw the dyeing, he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance and Islam’. So the man dyed with the black. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘A radiance, and Islam, and faith, and a love for your wives, and an awe in the hearts of your enemies’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Miskin ibn abu al-Hakam from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a man came to the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.

He (the Messenger of Allah) looked at the signs of oldness in his beard. The Holy Prophet said, ‘It is light.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) then said, ‘If one becomes white-headed because of oldness in Islam he will have a light on the Day of Judgment.’

The man applied dye to his hair with henna, then visited the Holy Prophet. On seeing him the Holy Prophet, said, ‘It is light and Islam.’ He then applied black dye to his hairs and the Holy Prophet, said, ‘It is light, Islam, belief and love from your women, and fear in the hearts of your enemies.’”
